claim: Antarctica has an island that keeps vanishing, and explorers keep renaming it.

end.title: Denman Glacier
end.description: Glacier in Queen Mary Land, Antarctica

knots.passage: This type of iceberg, also known as an ice island, can be quite large, as in the case of Pobeda Ice Island. Antarctic icebergs formed by breaking off from an ice shelf, such as the Ross Ice Shelf or Filchner–Ronne Ice Shelf, are typically tabular. The largest icebergs in the world are formed this way.
knots.hatnote: Flat-topped 'tabular' icebergs can grow big enough to pass for islands.

knots.passage: At this position, an ice island was first sighted by the United States Exploring Expedition, led by Charles Wilkes, in February 1840. It prevented his westward passage around the Antarctic coast, and he named it Termination Land. Douglas Mawson later renamed the island Termination Ice Tongue when he encountered it on the 1911–1913 Australasian Antarctic Expedition. No island was noted however at that location, when he returned during his 1929–1931 BANZARE expedition.
knots.hatnote: Off East Antarctica, one keeps turning up at the same spot.

knots.passage: A Soviet expedition came across the island in 1960 and renamed it again, this time as Pobeda Ice Island, named for Soviet victory over the Axis powers in the Great Patriotic War. They even established a temporary research station on the island, which existed between 9 May and 12 August 1960, alongside a few other stations named Mir on Drygalski Island and Druzhba on Zavadovsky Cupola, West Ice Shelf.
knots.hatnote: Then the Soviets found it again, gave it a third name, and moved in.

knots.passage: The ice island is created and vanishes periodically. It is created by the calving of an enormous block of ice from Denman Glacier, located in the eastern part of Shackleton Ice Shelf. The resulting tabular iceberg drifts northwest until it runs aground upon a shoal north of the ice shelf. The iceberg remains locked there in this position for a decade or more, until it has remodeled enough to free itself from the shoal. It then drifts into the open ocean, where it breaks into fragments.
knots.hatnote: So why does it keep coming and going?

knots.passage: The canyon under Denman Glacier has been found by the BedMachine Antarctica project (under the leadership of the University of California, Irvine) to be the deepest natural location on land (or at least not under liquid water) worldwide, with the bedrock being 3,500 m (11,500 ft) below sea level.
knots.hatnote: The glacier that makes the island sits on a record.

knots.passage: A 2020 study reported Denman Glacier has retreated 5.4 ± 0.3 km over a 20-year-period from 1996 to 2017–2018. The study projects that the glacier has the potential to undergo a rapid, irreversible retreat, due to the presence of a retrograde bed on the western flank of the glacier and the likely presence of warm water in the sub-ice-shelf cavity. If the entirety of the glacier were hollowed out, it would contribute to a 1.5 m rise in global sea level.
knots.hatnote: And the island-maker itself may not stay put.

payoff: The vanishing island is a stranded iceberg from Denman Glacier, a glacier over Earth's deepest land that may now be vanishing itself.
